acceptance: Every `benchbox run` and `run-official` UAT cell passes `--timeout` equal to its limit; the outside kill is at the limit plus 60 seconds.
A cell BenchBox stopped is `timed-out`; a cell the runner had to kill is `hung`; every reader of the token handles both.
description:
## Problem
Each UAT cell is bounded only from outside: the command line is built in tests/uat/matrix.py:295 (`benchbox run`) and :334 (`benchbox run-official`), assembled at tests/uat/runner.py:335-356, and killed through tests/uat/timeouts.py after `per_cell_timeout_s` (default 600). The outside kill reports status `timed-out` with a synthetic exit code 124 (`EXIT_TIMEOUT`). The diagnostic re-run keeps its own 180 s outside limit (runner.py:111-120). scripts/run_version_matrix.py has its own `cell_timeout_s`. A slow cell leaves no result saying it timed out.

## Owner decisions
"each cell passes `--timeout` equal to its cell limit, and the outside kill moves to the cell limit plus 60 seconds (the 30-second grace plus a margin). A slow cell then ends with a result that says 'timed out' and exit code 124, and is killed only if BenchBox hangs." Token: "keep `timed-out` for a cell BenchBox stopped at its limit; an outside kill becomes `hung` and is told apart by the runner's own 'I killed it' flag, not by the exit code. I update every reader of the token." ('I' is the agent.) Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
1. `run` and `run-official` cells pass `--timeout <cell limit>`; the outside limit becomes the cell limit plus 60 seconds. The diagnostic re-run gets the same treatment with its 180 s limit.
2. Classification uses `TimeoutResult.timed_out` (the runner killed it) for `hung`, and the product's exit code 124 for `timed-out`. An outside kill no longer reports a synthetic 124.
3. Update every reader of the status token: tests/uat/runner.py:510-515, rubric_fixtures.py:33, rubric.py:37, clickhouse_memory.py:251, _cli.py:600, orchestrator.py:693, cells_io.py:56, infrastructure_retry.py:19, scripts/release_reuse_uat_evidence.py:54; search again for any other.
4. scripts/run_version_matrix.py: pass `--timeout` and keep its outside limit with the same 60-second margin. CI `timeout-minutes` values are not touched.
5. UAT docs.

## Decision gates
A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). No change to which cells run, their limits, or pass and fail rules other than the new classification. How `hung` counts in retry and evidence-reuse rules: treat it exactly as `timed-out` was treated for an outside kill before this change, and list each rule in the pull request. No UAT run against live cloud.

## Verification rubric
Pass, each by a test that fails before the change: the `run` and `run-official` command lines carry `--timeout` equal to the cell limit and the outside limit is that plus 60; a stubbed cell exiting 124 is `timed-out`; a stubbed cell the runner killed is `hung` whatever its exit code; each listed reader handles `hung` (one assertion per reader); the version-matrix script passes `--timeout`. One real local cell through the lock-taking UAT entry point with a deliberately short limit ends `timed-out` with exit 124 and a marked bundle (announce command, maximum runtime, log path and stop condition; `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs`). `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents implement batch members and serial items under the delivery plan on run-timeout-plan-20261120 (owner, 2026-11-21); a batch member makes no tracker write, opens no pull request and stops at a landing report. A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
